$s = trim(fgets(STDIN));
$m = strlen($s);

// Build KMP automaton for pattern s
$alphabet = ['0', '1'];
$pi = array_fill(0, $m, 0);

for ($i = 1; $i < $m; $i++) {
    $j = $pi[$i - 1];
    while ($j > 0 && $s[$i] !== $s[$j]) {
        $j = $pi[$j - 1];
    }
    if ($s[$i] === $s[$j]) $j++;
    $pi[$i] = $j;
}

// Transition table: next[state][charIndex]
$next = array_fill(0, $m + 1, array_fill(0, 2, 0));
for ($state = 0; $state <= $m; $state++) {
    foreach ($alphabet as $idx => $ch) {
        if ($state < $m && $ch === $s[$state]) {
            $next[$state][$idx] = $state + 1;
        } else {
            if ($state == 0) {
                $next[$state][$idx] = 0;
            } else {
                $next[$state][$idx] = $next[$pi[$state - 1]][$idx];
            }
        }
    }
}
for ($idx = 0; $idx < 2; $idx++) {
    $next[$m][$idx] = $m;
}

// DP[pos][state][mask] where mask is bitmask of visited states (0..m-1)

$dp[0][0][1 << 0] = 1;

    $dp[$pos + 1] = array_fill(0, $m + 1, array_fill(0, $maxMask, 0));
    for ($state = 0; $state <= $m; $state++) {
        for ($mask = 0; $mask < $maxMask; $mask++) {
            $val = $dp[$pos][$state][$mask];
            if ($val == 0) continue;
            for ($bit = 0; $bit < 2; $bit++) {
                $ns = $next[$state][$bit];
                $nmask = $mask;
                if ($ns < $m) {
                    $nmask |= (1 << $ns);
                }
                $dp[$pos + 1][$ns][$nmask] += $val;
            }
        }
    }
}

// Count sequences where some visited state is accepting (state >= m)
$answer = 0;
for ($state = 0; $state <= $m; $state++) {
    for ($mask = 0; $mask < $maxMask; $mask++) {
        $val = $dp[$n][$state][$mask];
        if ($val == 0) continue;

        $ok = false;
        // Check if any visited state is accepting
        for ($st = 0; $st < $m; $st++) {
            if (($mask & (1 << $st)) == 0) continue;
            if ($st == $m) { // not possible since we don't set bit for m
                $ok = true;

            }
        }
        // Additionally, if final state is m, substring occurs
        if ($state == $m) $ok = true;

        if ($ok) $answer += $val;
    }

echo $answer . PHP_EOL;

        $j = $pi[$j - 1];
    }
    if ($s[$i] === $s[$j]) $j++;
    $pi[$i] = $j;
}

// transitions[state][bit] -> next_state
$trans = array_fill(0, $m + 1, [0, 0]);
for ($state = 0; $state < $m; $state++) {
    for ($b = 0; $b <= 1; $b++) {
        $c = $b ? '1' : '0';
        $j = $state;
        while ($j > 0 && $s[$j] !== $c) {
            $j = $pi[$j - 1];
        }
        if ($s[$j] === $c) $j++;
        $trans[$state][$b] = $j;
    }
}
// terminal state m stays at m
$trans[$m][0] = $m;
$trans[$m][1] = $m;

// DP[pos][state][mask] where mask is bitmask of length n: positions where pattern ends
// mask bit i corresponds to position i (0-based)
$sizeMask = 1 << $n;
$dp = [];
for ($i = 0; $i <= $n; $i++) {
    $dp[$i] = [];
    for ($st = 0; $st <= $m; $st++) {
        $dp[$i][$st] = array_fill(0, $sizeMask, 0);
    }
}
$dp[0][0][0] = 1;

for ($pos = 0; $pos < $n; $pos++) {
    for ($st = 0; $st <= $m; $st++) {
        $row = $dp[$pos][$st];
        for ($mask = 0; $mask < $sizeMask; $mask++) {
            $cnt = $row[$mask];
            if ($cnt == 0) continue;
            for ($b = 0; $b <= 1; $b++) {
                $nst = $trans[$st][$b];
                $nmask = $mask;
                if ($nst == $m) {
                    $nmask |= (1 << $pos);
                }
                $dp[$pos + 1][$nst][$nmask] += $cnt;
            }
        }
    }
}

// Precompute for each mask whether there exists a rotation where some end position
// gives a contiguous substring of length m (possibly wrapping)
$validMask = array_fill(0, $sizeMask, false);

for ($mask = 0; $mask < $sizeMask; $mask++) {
    if ($mask == 0) continue;
    // For each rotation shift r
    for ($r = 0; $r < $n && !$validMask[$mask]; $r++) {
        // For each position i where pattern ends
        for ($i = 0; $i < $n && !$validMask[$mask]; $i++) {
            if (!(($mask >> $i) & 1)) continue;
            // start index in original string
            $start = ($i - ($m - 1) + $n) % $n;
            // check if substring [start, start+m-1] exists in this rotation
            // rotation r means position k in rotated string corresponds to (k+r)%n in original
            // We need a k such that (k+r)%n == start
            // => k == (start - r + n) % n
            $k = ($start - $r + $n) % $n;
            // substring occupies positions k..k+m-1 in rotated string
            // always valid as indices wrap, so any end position is acceptable
            $validMask[$mask] = true;
        }
    }
}

$ans = 0;
for ($st = 0; $st <= $m; $st++) {
    for ($mask = 0; $mask < $sizeMask; $mask++) {
        if ($dp[$n][$st][$mask] == 0) continue;
        if ($validMask[$mask]) {
            $ans += $dp[$n][$st][$mask];
        }
    }
}

echo $ans . PHP_EOL;

// Read input
$n = intval(trim(fgets(STDIN)));
$s = trim(fgets(STDIN));
$m = strlen($s);

// Build KMP automaton for pattern s
$alphabet = ['0', '1'];
$pi = array_fill(0, $m, 0);

for ($i = 1; $i < $m; $i++) {
    $j = $pi[$i - 1];
    while ($j > 0 && $s[$i] !== $s[$j]) {
        $j = $pi[$j - 1];
    }
    if ($s[$i] === $s[$j]) $j++;
    $pi[$i] = $j;
}

// Transition function: next state for each state and bit
$next = array_fill(0, $m + 1, array_fill(0, 2, 0));
for ($state = 0; $state <= $m; $state++) {
    for ($b = 0; $b < 2; $b++) {
        if ($state == $m) {
            // Once matched, stay in matched state
            $next[$state][$b] = $m;
            continue;
        }
        $c = $b ? '1' : '0';
        $j = $state;
        while ($j > 0 && $c !== $s[$j]) {
            $j = $pi[$j - 1];
        }
        if ($c === $s[$j]) $j++;
        if ($j == $m) $next[$state][$b] = $m;
        else $next[$state][$b] = $j;
    }
}

// DP[pos][state][matched][firstBit][lastBit]
// matched: 0/1, firstBit: 0/1/2 (2 = undefined), lastBit: 0/1
// Use associative arrays to save memory
$DP = [];
// Initialize at position 0
$DP[0] = [];
$DP[0][0] = [];
$DP[0][0][0] = [];
$DP[0][0][0][2] = [];
$DP[0][0][0][2][0] = 1; // lastBit dummy when firstBit=2

for ($pos = 0; $pos < $n; $pos++) {
    if (!isset($DP[$pos])) continue;
    foreach ($DP[$pos] as $state => $byMatched) {
        foreach ($byMatched as $matched => $byFirst) {
            foreach ($byFirst as $firstBit => $byLast) {
                foreach ($byLast as $lastBit => $cnt) {
                    for ($b = 0; $b < 2; $b++) {
                        $newState = $next[$state][$b];
                        $newMatched = $matched || ($newState == $m);
                        if ($pos == 0) {
                            $newFirstBit = $b;
                            $newLastBit = $b;
                        } else {
                            $newFirstBit = $firstBit;
                            $newLastBit = $b;
                        }
                        if (!isset($DP[$pos + 1][$newState][$newMatched][$newFirstBit][$newLastBit])) {
                            $DP[$pos + 1][$newState][$newMatched][$newFirstBit][$newLastBit] = 0;
                        }
                        $DP[$pos + 1][$newState][$newMatched][$newFirstBit][$newLastBit] += $cnt;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

// Now enforce cyclic condition: consider wrap-around substring
// For each final state, we need to simulate continuing with firstBit as next bits
// up to length m-1 (since wrap can be at most m-1 chars from end to start)
$result = 0;
if (isset($DP[$n])) {
    foreach ($DP[$n] as $state => $byMatched) {
        foreach ($byMatched as $matched => $byFirst) {
            foreach ($byFirst as $firstBit => $byLast) {
                if ($firstBit === 2) continue; // should not happen for pos=n>0
                foreach ($byLast as $lastBit => $cnt) {
                    $hasMatch = $matched;
                    $curState = $state;
                    // simulate wrap-around using firstBit repeated (since only one bit known)
                    // but actual wrap-around can be any prefix; we only know first bit,
                    // so we must consider all possible prefixes of length up to m-1.
                    // Enumerate all possible prefixes of length up to m-1 explicitly.
                    // Since m <= 40, 2^(m-1) is too big, so we instead simulate all
                    // possible bit sequences via DP on automaton starting from curState.
                    // However, we only need to know if there exists some wrap that matches.
                    // For binary alphabet and small m, we can brute force all prefixes.
                    $wrapMatch = false;

                    // Precompute all prefixes up to length m-1
                    $maxLen = $m - 1;
                    if ($maxLen <= 0) {
                        // no wrap needed
                        $wrapMatch = false;
                    } else {
                        $limit = 1 << $maxLen;
                        for ($mask = 0; $mask < $limit && !$wrapMatch; $mask++) {
                            $st = $curState;
                            for ($len = 1; $len <= $maxLen; $len++) {
                                $bit = ($mask >> ($len - 1)) & 1;
                                $st = $next[$st][$bit];
                                if ($st == $m) {
                                    $wrapMatch = true;
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }

                    if ($hasMatch || $wrapMatch) {
                        $result += $cnt;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

echo $result . PHP_EOL;

            $j = $state;

                $j = $pi[$j - 1];
            }
            if ($c === $s[$j]) $j++;
            $next[$state][$bit] = $j;
        }
    }
}

$dp[0][0][0] = 1;

for ($pos = 0; $pos < $n; $pos++) {
    if (!isset($dp[$pos])) continue;
    foreach ($dp[$pos] as $state => $maskArr) {
        foreach ($maskArr as $mask => $cnt) {
            foreach ([0, 1] as $bit) {
                $ns = $next[$state][$bit];
                $nmask = $mask;

                $dp[$pos + 1][$ns][$nmask] += $cnt;
            }
        }
    }
}

// Count sequences where substring appears in some rotation
// A cyclic string t has s as substring in some rotation iff s appears in t+t
// but not necessarily in t itself. However, if s appears in t+t, then there is
// a position i < n where s starts; that corresponds to a contiguous substring
// in the linear string of length n with wrap-around. This is equivalent to
// having at least one occurrence in the circular sense.
// Our DP tracked occurrences in the linear string; to account for wrap,
